pr_body:
Fixes #84087
With user-defined functions introduced, backup/restore needs to work with the new function descriptors and schema descriptors containing function signatures. This commit adds logic into current backup/restore infrastructure to make sure function descriptors are properly backed up and restored.

Release note (enterprise change): backup/restore now can backup and restore user-defined function descriptors at database and cluster level.
Release justification: necessar fix to backup/restore to make sure it works with user-defined functions.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/87561)

@postamar thanks for the suggestion of using data driven test here, it helped me found 2 small bugs! I added data driven tests for both db backup/restore and cluster backup/restore. Instead of checking IDs, dependency behaviors on DROP/RENAME are tested. I found the existing data driven tests are mostly orthogonal so I didn't touch them, let me know if you have different opinion. I actually like to keep the two unit tests from earlier commit. I understand it'd be annoying that IDs are not stable when, for example, new system tables are added or other objects are added to the test. But I think it's a good idea to see the IDs actually match as an extra line of guard (since we're testing IDs rewritten).

Thanks, this looks good as far as I can tell. Perhaps add a test case to `TestCleanupDoesNotDeleteParentsWithChildObjects`? Just to check the behaviour is as expected when a restore fails. 

This release-blocker needs review by the Disaster Recovery team, please. CC @stevendanna @dt

> Thanks, this looks good as far as I can tell. Perhaps add a test case to `TestCleanupDoesNotDeleteParentsWithChildObjects`? Just to check the behaviour is as expected when a restore fails.

That's a good catch! udf was not dropped for failed restore. Fixed that and added test cases for it.

> I think we want to add a check for USAGE during backup here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/pkg/ccl/backupccl/backup_planning.go#L466
> 
Thanks for the review! that's a good catch on the privilege check, fixed with test cases :)

> Overall this looks reasonable to me. I suppose that UDFs may references tables that aren't being backed up, but that matches how we handle foreign keys and such currently.
>
The idea is that UDFs can only be backed up at db or cluster level. And we don' allow cross-db reference from a UDF, so that shouldn't be a concern.

issue_context.title: backupccl: make sure UDF descriptors are backed up and restored properly
issue_context.body:
A child of #58356

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. UDF descriptors should be properly backed up if they are referenced
2. Add logic to make sure objects on the UDF dependency graph exist. Dependency cycle detection should be added for the graph traversal.
4. Make sure UDF descriptor ids are properly rewritten like other descriptors
5. Make sure queries in UDF function body are properly rewritten with target database name
6. Make sure UDF OIDs referenced by tables/views are properly rewritten


Jira issue: CRDB-17455
Epic: CRDB-3405

review_comments: Is there any reason why these tests can't be implemented as data-driven tests? See `TestDataDriven`. This would be much more preferable. Also, I wouldn't count too much on individual ID values being stable over time, but that's a secondary concern.
I was a fool and didn't notice that's a thing for backup/restore :( Will move these tests there and add more tests.
Interesting, does this imply that restoring views with new_db_name wasn't quite right?
correct, if you're doing `BACKUP DATABASE xxx ..... WITH new_db_name = xxxx`, then db names in views are not rewritten. I'll add a test case for that actually, even it shares same code as udf.
